TFC.one_line: SE-U.S. regional bank: commercial, retail and wealth banking with a sticky low-cost deposit base.
TFC.reason: Cheap (9.7x fwd P/E) but ROE of 9% trails super-regional peers (USB, PNC) and growth is unexceptional; nothing here clears the bar for full diligence.
sources: triage_cards.csv data card; general knowledge of regional bank peer set

USB.one_line: Diversified super-regional bank with a strong payments (Elavon) and trust/wealth franchise.
USB.reason: Best ROE (12.6%) among peer regionals, double-digit revenue growth, and cheap at 10.5x forward earnings; payments scale is a real moat.

WFC.one_line: Money-center bank now unshackled from its 2018 asset cap, growing balance sheet again.
WFC.reason: Fed lifted the $1.95tn asset cap in June 2025; assets grew ~11% YoY in 2025 with improving revenue momentum, yet stock is only 10.6x forward earnings.

CBOE.one_line: Dominant U.S. options exchange (SPX/VIX products) with high-margin, volume-driven data/derivatives business.
CBOE.reason: 27% margins, 26% ROE and 23% revenue growth on a fair 17x forward multiple; options volume franchise is hard to replicate.

CME.one_line: World's largest derivatives exchange (rates, FX, ag, energy futures) with a self-reinforcing liquidity moat.
CME.reason: 63% margins and a near-unassailable clearing moat justify a look even though growth is soft this year (volumes/volatility subdued); fairly priced at 20.7x.

red_flags: Revenue down ~19% YoY and a $359.5M net loss in Q2 2026, the third consecutive earnings miss, as crypto spot volumes fell >20% industry-wide (BTC -14%, ETH -25%)
Earnings highly levered to crypto price cycle, not yet proven through a full downturn
COIN.one_line: Largest U.S. crypto exchange, diversifying into stablecoins, derivatives and prediction markets.
COIN.reason: Real market-share gains (10.3% of global volume) but revenue and profits are currently shrinking with the crypto cycle, and the stock is not statistically cheap; wait for the cycle to turn.

red_flags: Competitive pressure from Bloomberg, LSEG and AI-native research tools on organic ASV growth - worth checking in full diligence
FDS.one_line: Financial data/analytics platform (workstation, ESG, portfolio tools) sold on multi-year subscriptions with high switching costs.
FDS.reason: Cheap versus its own history at 13.8x forward with EPS growth of ~30%, though durability of that growth versus organic ASV trends needs verification.

red_flags: Net debt/EBITDA of 2.9x, elevated from the Black Knight mortgage-tech acquisition - integration/deleveraging pace worth checking
ICE.one_line: Exchanges (ICE futures, NYSE) plus fixed-income data and a mortgage-tech platform (Black Knight/MERS).
ICE.reason: 24% EPS growth and 38% margins at a reasonable 17.9x forward multiple; leverage from the Black Knight deal is the main thing to verify.

MCO.one_line: Global credit-rating duopolist (with S&P) plus a fast-growing analytics/research (MA) segment.
MCO.reason: 76.9% ROE and a near-regulatory moat in ratings; growth (20% eps) is real and the 25.5x multiple looks fair for the quality on offer.

MSCI.one_line: Global benchmark index provider (equity/fixed income indices, ESG, analytics) embedded in trillions of AUM.
MSCI.reason: 41% margins and near-universal index licensing create extreme switching costs; 25% eps growth at 25x is a fair price for a rare compounder.

red_flags: Net debt/EBITDA 2.6x post-Adenza deal - check deleveraging trajectory
NDAQ.one_line: Exchange operator transitioning into a market/regtech software business via the Adenza acquisition.
NDAQ.reason: 36% eps growth and 35% margins with the software mix shift underway; leverage from Adenza is the key diligence item.

SPGI.one_line: Credit ratings (with Moody's), Market Intelligence, Platts commodity data, and equity/bond indices with CME.
SPGI.reason: Duopoly ratings moat plus diversified data/indices businesses; 24% eps growth at 20.6x forward is a fair entry for this quality.

red_flags: $13.45bn AssuredPartners acquisition added ~$301M of GAAP integration costs, depressing trailing earnings and inflating the trailing P/E to 38x - normalize before comparing to peers
Net debt/EBITDA 3.0x, elevated versus historical norms from debt-funded M&A
AJG.one_line: Top-3 global insurance broker growing via disciplined tuck-in M&A plus the large AssuredPartners deal.
AJG.reason: Revenue growth of 31% (AssuredPartners plus organic) and a strong M&A track record; forward P/E of 16x looks cheap once one-time integration costs are stripped out, but leverage needs checking.

AON.one_line: Global insurance/reinsurance broker and HR/benefits consultant (one of three mega-brokers).
AON.reason: 44.7% ROE and durable recurring commission economics at only 14-15x forward earnings; organic growth (2.2% revenue) is the softest part of the story and worth checking.

BRO.one_line: Fast-growing insurance broker/wholesaler expanding organically and via bolt-on M&A.
BRO.reason: 32% revenue growth and 54% eps growth at just 12.8x forward is an attractive combination for a proven broker compounder.

red_flags: Stephenson v. Erie Indemnity: 3rd Circuit revived (Oct 14, 2025) a subscriber breach-of-fiduciary-duty suit over the 25% management fee; SCOTUS declined to review, so the case proceeds - a direct challenge to Erie's core fee-based economic model, though similar prior suits (Beltz, Ritz) were dismissed
ERIE.one_line: Manages Erie Insurance Exchange for a capped 25% management fee, with no underwriting risk of its own.
ERIE.reason: Extraordinary ROE (24.8%) and asset-light fee moat trade at only 20.2x trailing (cheap for ERIE's history), but ongoing subscriber litigation over the fee itself is a real overhang that full diligence must size.

MRSH.one_line: World's largest insurance broker and consulting group (Marsh, Guy Carpenter, Mercer, Oliver Wyman).
MRSH.reason: 25.9% ROE, durable recurring commissions, and 39% eps growth; 15.3x forward is fair for the largest, most diversified broker platform.

WTW.one_line: Global broker/consultant (risk, benefits, HR) in margin-improvement turnaround after the failed Aon merger.
WTW.reason: Post-merger-break turnaround delivering 41.5% eps growth and margin expansion, still cheap at 13.3x forward relative to peer brokers.

GS.one_line: Premier global investment bank: M&A/underwriting, trading, and a growing asset/wealth management arm.
GS.reason: 42.5% revenue growth from a strong trading/banking cycle, 16.9% ROE, at just 12.9x forward - cheap for the franchise quality.

red_flags: Crypto trading revenue fell 38% YoY in Q2 2026 as crypto markets cooled
Prediction/event-contract markets face ongoing regulatory scrutiny (state gaming regulators, CFTC) - monitor for adverse rulings
HOOD.one_line: Retail brokerage expanding aggressively into options, crypto, prediction markets and international wealth management.
HOOD.reason: Revenue and eps growth near 30-50% and rapidly improving profitability justify a look despite a rich 45.6x forward P/E, but the crypto/prediction-market revenue mix is volatile and regulator-dependent.

IBKR.one_line: Low-cost, highly automated global electronic brokerage serving active traders and institutions.
IBKR.reason: 24% ROE and 27% revenue growth with a durable low-cost/tech moat; 29x forward is a fair price for the growth on offer.

MS.one_line: Investment bank plus the largest wealth-management platform (E*TRADE, Morgan Stanley advisors) among peers.
MS.reason: 28% revenue growth as the wealth-management pivot pays off, at a reasonable 14.6x forward multiple.

RJF.one_line: Regional wealth-management and investment-banking firm known for advisor retention and a conservative culture.
RJF.reason: 24% eps growth and 18.4% ROE at just 11.3x forward is attractively priced for a consistently well-run franchise.

SCHW.one_line: Largest U.S. discount brokerage/custodian, still realizing scale benefits from the TD Ameritrade integration.
SCHW.reason: 43% eps growth and 38.8% margins as integration synergies flow through, at only 13.3x forward earnings.

red_flags: Aflac Japan (the bulk of earnings) is in secular decline - shrinking in-force block, FX headwinds; forward eps growth is -18.6% and revenue is -1%
AFL.one_line: Supplemental health/life insurer, primarily in Japan, with a U.S. voluntary-benefits business.
AFL.reason: Fairly priced for a business with a shrinking core Japan block; not a case of an undervalued grower, so it does not clear the bar despite a reasonable multiple.
sources: triage_cards.csv data card; general knowledge of Aflac Japan block dynamics

red_flags: FCF yield of -33.7% and volatile net margin (4.6%) typical of a large life insurer's reserve/mark-to-market accounting - needs GAAP-vs-statutory unpacking
MET.one_line: Global life/group benefits/retirement insurer (MetLife, Brighthouse legacy ties) with modest structural ROE.
MET.reason: Cheap at 9.2x forward, but the eps rebound looks like normalization off a weak prior-year comp rather than durable acceleration, and ROE (13%) is unexceptional for the sector.

PFG.one_line: Retirement, group benefits and asset-management (Principal) provider serving small/mid-size businesses.
PFG.reason: Cheap at 11.3x forward with a strong momentum print, but this looks like a steady, average-quality insurer rather than a standout on quality or durable growth.

PRU.one_line: Large diversified life insurer and asset manager (PGIM) with U.S. and international operations.
PRU.reason: Very cheap at 8.1x forward, but the large eps growth figure likely reflects normalization against a soft comp rather than a genuine growth acceleration; ROE (12%) is unremarkable.

BRK-B.one_line: Diversified holding company (insurance float, railroads, energy, equities) now led by Greg Abel as CEO.
BRK-B.reason: Best-in-class balance sheet and capital allocation; the Buffett-to-Abel CEO transition (completed, Buffett remains chairman) was well-telegraphed and is not a disqualifying risk.
sources: general knowledge: Berkshire succession announced 2025, Abel became CEO

AIG.one_line: Global commercial P&C insurer, post-Corebridge-spinoff, returning capital via buybacks.
AIG.reason: Cheap at 8.6x forward, but ROE of only 7.2% is still below cost of capital, and the large eps jump looks like a rebound rather than a proven structural improvement.

L.one_line: Diversified holding company (CNA Financial insurance, Boardwalk Pipeline, Loews Hotels) trading at a discount to NAV.
L.reason: Eps growth of -64% likely reflects a tough comp against a prior one-time gain; low ROE (9%) and no clear growth or quality edge keep this out of full diligence.
